name: French Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "France" = 539,100 km2 on the sphere; metropolitan France in 1870 incl. Savoy and Nice (1860) ~543,000 km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1870 = 38,440k; 1866 census 38.07M (incl. Savoy and Nice, excl. Algeria).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) France 1870 = 39.7% (high); 1872 census urban (communes with 2,000+ agglomerated) 31%; towns of 5,000+ ~22-25%.

activePersonnel.note: Franco-Prussian War infobox: 492,585 active including 300,000 reservists (Howard 1991 p. 39; Clodfelter). COW milper 1869 = 474,000, 1870 = 452,000. Mid = army present with the colours in late July 1870 as reservists straggled in, plus navy.

trainedReserves.note: Garde Mobile 417,366 (page, Howard p. 39; nominal 400,000, largely untrained) plus reservists not yet joined. The Government of National Defence later raised far more (total deployment 2,000,740).

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery and train ~40,000, engineers ~7,000, gendarmerie ~20,000, navy and marine infantry ~30,000 effective. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total French deployment 2,000,740 (Clodfelter via page) of 38.4M = 5.2% over the war.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 100 line regiments and the Imperial Guard; Army of the Rhine ~200,000 infantry at the outbreak, plus depots, Algeria and the Rome garrison.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Chassepot breech-loader, 1,037,555 in inventory, range ~1,500 m (page, Wawro 2002 p. 102)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service veterans of Crimea, Italy and Mexico; reservists poorly integrated

count.note: 20 chasseur a pied battalions, Zouaves and Tirailleurs algeriens.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Armee d'Afrique veterans

count.note: 10 cuirassier and 2 carabinier regiments plus Guard cuirassiers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: cuirasses useless against rifles (Reichshoffen charges)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: brave, tactically obsolete

count.note: Dragoons, lancers, chasseurs, hussars, Chasseurs d'Afrique and Spahis.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: good horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: neglected reconnaissance

count.note: Wawro, The Franco-Prussian War (2003) ch. 3: the Army of the Rhine had ~924 field guns and ~190 mitrailleuses; with depots and other commands ~1,300 field pieces. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: bronze rifled muzzle-loading La Hitte guns with time fuses, outranged by Krupp steel breech-loaders (page)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: slow, ammunition-sparing doctrine (page)

count.note: Conway's 1860-1905: ~16-17 seagoing ironclad frigates, ~7 ironclad corvettes, ~20 coast-defence ironclads and floating batteries, plus wooden screw frigates. Second-largest fleet in the world. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Gloire lineage, armoured frigates

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: naval reservists sent ashore to Paris and the Garde Mobile (page)

count.note: Educated guess: avisos, gunboats and transports.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: large colonial gunboat force

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Napoleon III, Bazaine and MacMahon; chaotic mobilisation (page: reservists choked the railway stations)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-service regiments with strong identity; Garde Mobile mutinous

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: confident after Crimea and Italy, war fever in Paris in July 1870

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: Chassepot and the mitrailleuse ahead of Prussia; artillery behind

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: large ironclad fleet

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Metz detached forts, Paris enceinte and forts, Belfort

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: dense rail net but chaotic mobilisation (page; Howard p. 68)

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: telegraph; balloons out of besieged Paris

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: cavalry did not scout; balloons in Paris

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1869 = 23,912, 1870 = 59,066. Against a national product of ~900M pounds: 2.7% in peace, ~6.5% in the war year.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Toutain/Marczewski accounts put industry near 30% of French product around 1870.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, France agriculture share of employment 1866 = 51.0%, 1886 = 47.0%; interpolated 1870 = ~50.2%. s = 1 assumed: near self-sufficient in grain. Mid 1 - 0.50 = 0.50; range a 0.47-0.53. audit 2026-10-30: was 0.25/0.35/0.45, which contradicted the note's own farm share of about half; recomputed with the formula.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. French conscription classes of the 1860s numbered ~320,000 men.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field-gun output per year; the Government of National Defence improvised much more in 1870-71.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ironclads launched per year at Toulon, Brest, Cherbourg, Lorient and La Seyne.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: routes nationales ~38,000 km and departementales ~47,000 km, plus chemins vicinaux.

railKm.note: CHAT railline France: 1869 = 16,465 km, 1870 = 15,544 km (the 1870 value appears to exclude the lines lost with Alsace-Lorraine). Mid includes them.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Brest, Toulon, Cherbourg, Lorient, Rochefort, Marseille, Le Havre, Bordeaux, Saint-Nazaire, Dunkirk.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 1,072k tons (France 1870, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: army tied to rail depots; supply breakdown at Metz in August 1870.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: about 3M horses plus mules and donkeys.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: fortress belt (Metz, Strasbourg, Belfort, Paris) and population support; no harsh-climate depth.

notes: Snapshot = French Empire at the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War (declared 19 July 1870), forces as mobilisation was under way. Population and territory = metropolitan France incl. Savoy and Nice; Algeria and colonies excluded; includes is empty. Personnel: regular army with reservists who had joined and the navy = active; Garde Mobile and reservists not yet joined = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Franco-Prussian War page (Howard 1991 p. 39; Clodfelter 2017 p. 184; Wawro). Branch split is a reconstruction (grade C).
